history.origins: Rikken originates in the southern Netherlands, mainly the province of Noord Brabant, and is also played in Belgium. It is a plain trick game with trumps and bidding, with similarities to Solo Whist, and is played in competitions.
timeline: 20th century: documented in Netherlands and Belgium as regional variant of Solo Whist.
history.cultural: Regional favourite in Noord Brabant and Belgian card-playing circles; played in competitions.

rules.objective: Fulfill contract. Rik: 8 tricks with called Ace partner. Solo: 8-13 tricks alone. MisÃ¨re: 0 tricks. Piek: exactly 1 trick.
rules.gameplay: 1. Bidding: left of dealer first; must bid higher or pass; three passes ends. 2. Declarer names trump (if applicable), calls Ace for partner (Rik/Rik Beter). 3. Play: follow suit; trump beats non-trump. 4. Scoring: base + overtricks or undertricks.
keyRules: Rik: call Ace for partner; 8 tricks. Rik Beter: hearts always trump.
8-13 Alleen: solo, choose trump. Open variants: hand face-up after first trick.
MisÃ¨re/Piek: no trump. Cards never shuffled between hands.
